narrative: Material PL1__MF1B2004 exhibits erratic demand (CV=0.431) across 115 working days with a mean of 751 units/day and no significant trend. Lead times are unstable (CV=0.443, mean=2.97 days), and their variability dominates the buffer requirement at 76.1% of total variance. The current SAP policy of safety stock=0 and MOQ=60 generates ~4,559 annual orders at extreme ordering cost; the recommended (r,Q) policy with Q=4,900 and SS=1,892 reduces total annual cost by 96.6% while achieving a 95% service level and staying well within storage capacity.
warnings: Lead time CV > 0.4 indicates unstable supplier performance; safety stock is elevated accordingly.
SAP safety stock of 0 provides no buffer against demand/lead-time variability — stockout risk is high under current policy.

research_insights.selection_rationale: Demand is near-continuous (97% non-zero working days) making a continuous-review model superior to periodic review. The (r,Q) policy with EOQ-derived order quantity minimises total inventory costs while the reorder point absorbs lead-time and demand uncertainty at the target service level.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Storage capacity is not binding: max post-replenishment stock of 6,792 units uses only 37.5% of the 18,133-unit limit. No capacity-driven order reduction required.
